Locations included Bozeman, Conrad, Corvallis, Huntley, Moccasin, Richland, and Sidney MT. Climate Chickpea is a cool season crop that grows best when daytime temperatures are between 70 and 84 °F, and nighttime temperatures are between 64 and 70 °F. The crop does well in regions with 6-10 inches of growing season precipitation. Temperatures above 98 °F can cause stress during early flowering and pod development, resulting in reduced yields. But chickpea performs better than dry pea and lentil under heat and drought stress. Chickpea as a crop is somewhat drought tolerant. Cultural Practices Soil Chickpea grows best on well drained soils with a neutral pH. It is not well adapted to saline soils and does not tolerate wet or waterlogged soils.
